releases.summary: Resilient Doctor diagnostics and explicit preserved-Hub compatibility checks.

changes.text: Prevented missing or concurrently unavailable repository paths from crashing Doctor, status, bridge inspection, or command capture; affected checks now return deterministic structured findings.

Added a versioned generated-Hub capability contract and read-only compatibility checker with exact capability probes, managed migration scope, protected user-state exclusions, and fail-closed fallback behavior.
Made setup, review, repository-bridge, and upgrade skills check the Hub capabilities they require before relying on newer commands or documents.

migration: Start a fresh Codex task after upgrading so the updated Doctor, compatibility, and skill guidance load.
Existing generated Hubs are preserved and are not automatically regenerated or migrated.
When a required capability is unavailable, use the reported plan-and-diff migration scope; plugin upgrade alone does not modify the Hub.

releases.summary: Opt-in durable Missions for bounded multi-task coordination in the Codex task control room.

changes.text: Added ignored local MissionRecord parents that link exact verified persistent Codex tasks without replacing their owning projects or creating a separate dashboard.

Added dispatch_only, watch_only, and supervised modes with required and optional DAG nodes, declared input and output-reference types, controlled fan-in, bounded budgets, explicit stop conditions, and operator-only completion.

Added Mission commands for graph management, exact dispatch receipts, compact sync planning and apply, deterministic checkpoint/status derivation, typed next actions, two-phase outbox delivery, reconciliation, failure recording, and explicit close.

Added an injected Codex UI task-adapter contract covering exact project and task identity, non-waitable clientThreadId-only pending dispatch, paired clientThreadId and resolved-task reconciliation, unknown-create handling, wait batching of at most eight exact task/host targets, and opaque per-task cursors; pending or unknown JIT results preserve the exact prepared action without authorizing duplicate create.
Preserved ordinary Flightdeck dispatch as receipt-and-stop by default; Mission observation or supervision occurs only after explicit user opt-in.

Treated child commentary and final text as untrusted display-only material and limited final child output to closed bounded output_declarations; children never receive or author producer task bindings, resolver identity, or canonical artifact/task refs.

Kept commit, push, pull request or comment, publication, deployment, shared-environment mutation, external communication, compliance submission, risk acceptance, and closure behind their existing explicit approval boundaries in every Mission mode.

Hardened Mission authorization validation to require exact authorization_boundary equality across the parent, every producer and consumer node, and every outbox action; made the boundary a required top-level action field included in idempotency and revalidated throughout the action lifecycle.
Rejected non-regular, unreadable, or oversized observation inputs before reading or parsing them, with filesystem and post-read max_forwarded_bytes checks.

Separated tool-derived Mission state from final child outcomes: nonterminal observations forbid outcomes, review_ready and failed_validation require exact normalized outcomes, and fan-in requires review_ready with passed validation and non-empty output declarations that core can materialize.
Documented the persisted generated Mission defaults: 50 units, 3 retries, 200 actions, 65536 forwarded bytes, 604800 seconds duration, 3600 seconds before stale, and a 2097152-byte record.

Made Mission graphs planning-only and frozen after any dispatch, pending or unknown receipt, observation, or outbox state; newly discovered owners require a proposed new Mission and user approval, while a declared non-root dispatch requires its exact prepared core action with the complete parent set and refs exactly equal to the complete eligible accepted set with at least one per parent.
Clarified that typed references are control-plane metadata rather than artifact transport, requiring proven consumer resolvability, planning-time co-location where compatible, or a fail-closed stop.
Standardized recommended domain reference identifiers and required independent review to use a persistent runtime task distinct from the producer under review.

Persisted unique bounded success criteria as ordered criterion-001 records, repeatable per-node --criterion-id assignments, and exact ordered terminal criterion_results with passed, failed, blocked, or degraded dispositions; required nodes must cover every criterion before dispatch and every required assignment must pass before fan-in.

Replaced caller-supplied Mission boundaries with repeatable closed six-field --authorized-target-json records and a core-derived scope-<48hex> boundary over canonical Mission ID, targets, criteria, and non-goals; node targets and actions are revalidated without treating the token as authority.

Made core materialize canonical artifact/task refs only after an exact persisted producer receipt, using bounded child artifact or own-task declarations; artifact namespaces contain resolver, producer node, unpadded base64url task binding, lowercase declaration SHA, and artifact ID, while resolver metadata is present only for transported artifacts.

Added required normalized display-only observation status_code values and bounded per-criterion status codes; final codes must equal child outcome codes, intermediate states remain outcome-less, review_ready requires every assigned criterion passed, and failed_validation requires at least one unmet criterion.

Required every declared dependency ready and action dependency_node_ids equal to the complete parent list; planned handoffs prepare before JIT create, client-only or unknown results preserve the prepared action as non-actionable, exact task/runtime/host reconciliation records awaiting_handoff, and acknowledgement transitions to ordinary running.

Bound every sync apply to the exact plan_token returned by sync plan, covering Mission generation, input digest, observation and event identity, accepted and ignored changes, rendered actions, and resulting state; locked recomputation rejects drift.

Closed observation/action identity with persisted event_digest over normalized accepted declarations and criterion results, a trigger_digest bound to producer event ID, event digest, and status, and whole-record recomputation of idempotency_key and action-<prefix> ID.

Restricted automated cross-node handoff to core-materialized artifact: or codex-task: references; child-declared check: and review: remain terminal operator evidence, and no child or adapter may bootstrap or repair producer provenance. This is provenance control, not content transport.

Defaulted multi-component development Missions to a contract-first graph, with integration depending directly on the contract and every implementation and independent review depending directly on every producer it must inspect.
Routed ordinary security-focused change and readiness review through flightdeck-review and reserved codex-security:security-scan for explicit repository or scoped-path security-scan intent.

Made CI, platform, compliance, research, and professional-artifact examples use child artifact declarations followed by core-materialized refs; terminal check/review declarations remain operator-only, and blocked or stale producers stop handoff.

Added generated-Hub Mission compatibility capabilities, migration-safe upgrade guidance that preserves declarations, materialized refs, event digests, and awaiting-handoff state, plus installed acceptance fields for core materialization, child canonical-ref rejection, and blocked/stale non-actionability.

Removed resume from the Mission action allowlist. Only a prepared planned consumer with an exact receipt in internal awaiting_handoff may receive dependency delivery; genuine blocked, derived stale, pending, and unknown consumers are non-actionable stops.

Defined three closed child output declaration forms: artifact {type, artifact_id, digest}, producer task {type, codex_task: true}, and terminal {type, ref, digest} restricted to check: or review:. Core persists both declarations and its materialized refs.

Prevented duplicate JIT creation after a clientThreadId-only receipt by preserving the exact prepared handoff with dispatch_pending until paired client/task reconciliation; pending or unknown unresolved actions may be failed explicitly but remain non-actionable and are never retried.

Closed the non-root dispatch bypass: record-dispatch now requires exactly one matching prepared dependency_handoff with every declared parent and refs equal to the complete eligible core-materialized accepted set with at least one per parent, so terminal check/review or incompatible refs cannot start dependents.

migration: Start a fresh Codex task after upgrading so the Flightdeck Mission skill and updated coordination guidance load.
